post_title: How many drones will Ukraine's Air Force report Russia launched at Ukraine on the night of 12–13 November 2026?

question.title: How many drones will Ukraine's Air Force report Russia launched at Ukraine on the night of 12–13 November 2026?
question.description:
Russia runs a continuous long-range drone and missile campaign against Ukraine, and the autumn of 2026 has seen it intensify: the UN Commission of Inquiry reported on 26 October 2026 on "systematic waves of attacks with hundreds of drones and missiles at a time", and President Zelensky said more than 170 strikes on Ukrainian energy infrastructure were recorded between 11 and 22 October 2026 as winter approaches.

The Ukrainian Air Force publishes a nightly report on its Telegram channel (https://t.me/s/kpszsu) each morning, typically between 07:30 and 10:00 Kyiv time, stating how many drones were launched at Ukraine "starting from 18:00" the previous day, which drone types were used (Shahed-type, jet-powered variants, Gerbera, S8000 Banderol/Dan-T, Parodiya decoys) and how many were shot down or suppressed. English-language summaries appear each morning via outlets such as Ukrinform (e.g. https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-ato/4179592-air-defenses-down-three-missiles-96-drones-used-by-russia-to-attack-ukraine-overnight.html) and Ukrainska Pravda.

This question uses drone counts rather than missile counts because, since 11 August 2026, the Air Force no longer publishes how many ballistic missiles Russia fired or how many were intercepted in these morning reports — it names missile types only, except when a single missile was used (https://kyivindependent.com/ukraines-air-force-faces-backlash-as-it-stops-publishing-russian-ballistic-missile-figures). Drone launch totals, by contrast, are still published precisely every night.

Recent nightly launch totals from those reports: 165 (night of 19–20 Oct), 126 (23–24 Oct), 140 (25–26 Oct), 280 (26–27 Oct), 88 (27–28 Oct), 112 (28–29 Oct) and 113 (29–30 Oct). The largest single night of the campaign so far was 14–15 October 2026, when the Air Force reported 580 attack drones and decoys launched, of which 536 were neutralised (https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1220461.html). Daytime waves are reported separately and have reached 138 drones (15 Oct). Jet-powered drones make up a large and growing share of launches: Air Force spokesperson Yurii Ihnat said Russia used 3,177 jet-powered drones in September 2026 versus 2,850 in August, part of a rising monthly trend. Useful forecasting inputs include Russian drone production and stockpiles, the observed spacing of large "wave" nights, the jet-powered share (which strains Ukrainian air defences amid an interceptor shortage), weather, and the state of the energy campaign.

question.resolution_criteria: This question resolves using the Ukrainian Air Force's overnight report for the night of 12–13 November 2026, published on the Air Force's official Telegram channel (https://t.me/s/kpszsu) on the morning of 13 November 2026 (Kyiv time). The answer is the single figure that report gives for the total number of drones (UAVs) launched at Ukraine during that night — the report's headline launch count (for example, if it states that Russia attacked with 152 attack drones, the answer is 152); separately listed subtypes or decoy/imitator categories are not added to that headline figure, and the number of drones shot down, suppressed or lost is not used. If the report states only a combined total of air attack means without a separate drone figure, the answer is that combined total minus any missile count stated in the same report, or otherwise the drone figure for that night reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions). The figure used is the latest one the Air Force publishes for that night before 18:00 Kyiv time on 13 November 2026. If no overnight report is published for that night, the answer is the Air Force's figure for that night as reported by [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions), and is 0 if no drone launches against Ukraine that night are reported.
question.fine_print: "Night of 12–13 November 2026" means the overnight period covered by the report published on the morning of 13 November 2026 — normally the period beginning at 18:00 Kyiv time on 12 November 2026. If that report defines its window differently or merges evening and overnight counts, the figure it presents as its overnight drone launch total applies. Drones launched later on 13 November 2026, which the Air Force covers in separate daytime reports, do not count.
